newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end higher on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bond prices closed higher across the board on Tuesday in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.
"Bond prices were marked up slightly today following a fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.25/98.35 compared with Monday's close of S$98.15/98.20, May 2002 at S$99.40/99.50 against S$99.25/99.30 and June 2003 at S$94.45/94.55 from S$94.28/94.33.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent from Monday's 4-1/4 4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 3.07/3.02 percent versus Monday's yield of 3.37/3.32 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.73/2.68 percent against 2.86/2.81 percent.
